overview.central_question: How can a person externalize a mental model so an AI can understand the whole pattern before inspecting individual concepts?
overview.pattern: Mindfield is a spatial discussion: a cyan core premise branches into interface intent, reuse across projects, and possible runtime forms.

bubbles.title: What is Mindfield?
bubbles.detail: Mindfield is a spatial reasoning surface: a person externalizes a mental model as connected concepts, and an AI can inspect, question, extend, and reuse the same graph as structured thought.

bubbles.title: Design language
bubbles.detail: A visual system that makes complexity feel calm.

bubbles.title: AI context
bubbles.detail: Structured context that stays legible to both humans and models.

bubbles.title: Open question
bubbles.detail: What should this become when the structure changes?

bubbles.title: Next move
bubbles.detail: Turn a promising thread into something testable.

bubbles.title: How should this feel?
bubbles.detail: The human adaptation should feel like a calm 3D discussion: spatial bubbles, minimal chrome, direct editing, and gestures that preserve the feeling of thinking in a field.

bubbles.title: How do we use this elsewhere?
bubbles.detail: Use Mindfield as a portable reasoning layer for other work: capture concepts here, connect their meaning, then let a project-specific tool read the graph instead of rebuilding context from scratch.

bubbles.title: VS Code integration
bubbles.detail: Package Mindfield as a reusable workspace companion: open the graph beside code, expose project context to agents, and persist the graph in the repository so setup is not repeated.

bubbles.title: Web or local app
bubbles.detail: Start as a local-first web app with a portable graph file. A future hosted mode can sync graphs, but the canonical document should remain inspectable and usable without a service.
